Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented the first real `GrpcConnectionCount` pool boundary. Rust now opens that many independently connected Tonic TiKV channels per store and `KvRpcClient` selects them in client-go's exact `atomic.Add(...)+mod` order (first selection is index 1). The deterministic lazy-channel regression proves the rotation without a live server. Batch streams, pool closure/recreation, monitor state, forwarding, and error lifecycle remain part of the unfinished atomic `internal/client` receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the pooled bidirectional `BatchCommands` transport primitive. It selects the next source-compatible pooled TiKV channel and returns Tonic's generated response stream from an arbitrary request stream. It deliberately owns neither request IDs nor response correlation; those are the next `client_batch.go` state-machine layers. The primitive is warning-clean but not yet called by production code, so it is seed evidence only.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added source-derived batch-loop prerequisites: a monotonic request-ID allocator that starts at 1 (zero is never in flight), and a one-shot pending-response registry that publishes IDs before send, delivers one response exactly once, and ignores outdated duplicate responses. Focused regressions pass. These remain unintegrated seeds until the batch send/receive stream loop owns their cancellation, timeout, forwarding, and failure paths.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited the batch-stream failure and receive invariants in `client_batch.go`. Entries are published before send; a send error only fails its exact IDs because the send can be ambiguous and later responses become outdated. Stream failure only retires pending entries for the failed forwarding destination; forwarding peers may still respond. Receive processing must pair request IDs and responses, skip canceled entries, retire each entry once, track highest received ID, and treat missing entries as outdated. These rules preclude a generic error clone/fail-all helper in Rust and define the required owned batch state machine.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): implemented the source `batchCommandsBuilder` selection layer as the crate-private `store::batch` seed. It converts typed command wrappers only after priority selection, preserves direct versus per-forwarded-host request groups, allocates source-compatible IDs monotonically across `reset`, skips pre-selection cancellation without spending an ID, and lets priorities at least 10 exceed the normal configured batch limit. Three focused regressions cover grouping/IDs, priority-limit behavior, and cancellation. This is explicitly not yet a `client_batch.go` receipt: selected entries still require publication, response registration, post-send cancellation, stream ownership/recreation, and forwarding-aware failures in one integrated lifecycle.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected and extended the pending-response seed to preserve source receive/failure outcomes. A dropped caller receiver now retires as `Cancelled`, distinct from a missing/duplicate `Outdated` ID; conversion failures can be delivered to one response without poisoning the stream; send failure retires only its explicit IDs; and stream failure retires only entries with the same direct/forwarded host. The focused regressions cover all three terminal response dispositions and prove a failed direct stream does not fail a live forwarded entry. Stream opening and lifecycle integration remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the source receive-loop correlation seed. `store::batch::receive_batch_response` pairs each response ID with its generated response, retires exactly once through the pending registry, records the largest received ID, and distinguishes delivered/cancelled/outdated outcomes. It leaves unrelated sibling responses live if one oneof conversion fails; a malformed response with fewer payloads than IDs returns a safe internal protocol error before retirement, where Go's unchecked index would panic. Focused regressions cover mixed terminal outcomes and per-response conversion failure. Owning timing/load metrics and a live stream loop remain pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the metadata half of the pooled `BatchCommands` stream primitive. Each Tonic stream now carries client-go's exact `tikv-forwarded-host` value when forwarding and always carries `tikv-batch-conn-index` for its selected source-compatible pool slot. The metadata is applied during stream creation rather than per request, matching Go's gRPC-stream constraint; a focused regression covers direct and forwarded streams. A live stream/client lifecycle remains pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added an owned BatchCommands stream/dispatcher seed. It retains caller response senders through builder selection, registers every concrete ID before sending its protobuf group, retires only that group's IDs when the outbound stream closes, and isolates receive/stream failures by forwarding host. A dispatcher chooses exactly one pooled connection index per nonempty builder pass and creates direct/forwarded streams on that same slot, matching client-go's `getClientAndSend` topology; empty flushes do not advance the pool. Focused publication and host-isolation regressions plus the 270-test nightly library suite pass. This remains an in-progress lifecycle slice: adaptive batch waiting, max-concurrency admission, stream recreation, timing/load metrics, shutdown, and typed request-path integration still require the rest of `internal/client`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the deterministic `turboBatchTrigger` policy state from `client_batch.go`: basic/standard/positive presets, Go-compatible `custom`/bare-JSON parsing and fallback, time/probability smoothing, capped arrival intervals, and fractional batch-wait-size selection. The source-derived regression covers every preset plus custom and invalid parsing; the full pinned-nightly library suite now passes 271 tests. The trigger is not yet connected to an async request-collection loop, so this remains a prerequisite rather than a claim that adaptive batching is complete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited source stream recreation against the Rust retry substrate. `client_batch.go` fails only the affected forwarding host, then uses an unbounded `BoTiKVRPC` backoffer while the batch client is live; Rust's source-mapped `RetryBackoffer` already provides the same TiKV-RPC class and cancellation-aware wait. Correct integration requires the dispatcher/stream owner to gain an explicit cancellation/close lifecycle first, so a reconnect task can stop deterministically instead of becoming an unbounded detached loop. No speculative retry loop was added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added that explicit batch-stream cancellation ownership. Every owned stream receives a child cancellation token; dispatcher close rejects subsequent flushes, cancels running receive tasks, clears owned streams, and fails only builder entries that never acquired a concrete request ID. Published entries remain in the pending transport registry rather than being generically failed, preserving the source queued-versus-in-flight distinction. The focused close regression and the 272-test full nightly library suite pass. This establishes the stop condition required for source-compatible retry/recreation, which remains the next lifecycle integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added source `MaxConcurrencyRequestLimit` admission to the dispatcher seed. Normal selection is limited by `min(requested, maxConcurrency - publishedPending)`, where the pending registry is the ownership-safe equivalent of client-go's `sent` count; saturation clamps to zero. The existing builder still admits high-priority entries at zero normal capacity, preserving `getClientAndSend` behavior. The focused regression and the 273-test full nightly library suite pass. Config-to-dispatcher wiring still awaits typed request-path integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the RawKV shared-budget topology audit from `rawkv.go`. `BatchGet`/`BatchDelete` and `BatchPut` do not delegate their retry ownership to a generic region plan: they create one 20,000-ms operation backoffer, fork a batch parent, fork once per region batch, cancel sibling forks on the first error, then call `UpdateUsingForked` with the last completed child. Single-key and scan loops create their own 20,000-ms operation backoffer and retain it through region lookup/send/region-error retry. Rust's generic `RetryableMultiRegion` clones a legacy attempt-count strategy instead, so its replacement must be a RawKV-owned orchestration migration with this complete cancellation/merge receipt—not a mutex-wrapped `RetryBackoffer` or an unrelated transaction-plan change.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): enabled and regenerated Tonic server bindings through the owned `proto-build` generator (`build_server(true)`). The prior generation emitted only clients, which made a Rust equivalent of client-go's `internal/client/mockserver` unrepresentable without a hand-written transport shim. All generated protobuf server modules now compile on the pinned nightly. This is generated test-infrastructure enablement only: the source mockserver's request hooks, batch behavior, and failure scenarios remain separate work and no package receipt is claimed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the source inventory for `internal/logutil` (`log.go`, `tracing.go`, and `hex.go`, with no package tests). The key remaining behavior is not ordinary logging: Go `Hex(proto.Message)` uses runtime protobuf reflection to recursively render/redact all byte fields. Prost-generated Rust types currently have no retained runtime descriptors, so completion needs a descriptor/reflection design or generated per-message formatting. A Debug-format approximation would expose a different redaction contract and was intentionally not added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added a real in-process Tonic transport regression for the owned `BatchCommands` dispatcher. A narrow test-only router serves the generated `/tikvpb.Tikv/BatchCommands` method (rather than inventing a full TiKV service), echoes `Empty` requests, and records metadata. The production dispatcher sends one direct and one forwarded request through actual protobuf streaming; both receive their correctly correlated response, and the server observes distinct forwarding metadata with the same source-selected connection index. This validates the seed’s wire boundary and metadata placement, not mockserver parity or reconnect/metrics/collection lifecycle behavior.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added cancellation-owned stream recreation to the BatchCommands seed. On a receive failure or clean stream end, the receive loop retires only that forwarding host’s pending entries, clears its outbound sender under the same lock used for request publication, and the supervisor recreates the metadata-bearing stream with the source-mapped `BO_TIKV_RPC` backoff. New publication waits for that replacement rather than writing to an obsolete generation. The in-process Tonic regression closes the first stream after its response, then proves a subsequent request succeeds through a replacement. Streams on the same selected pool slot share a reconnection gate held through retries, mapping client-go's connection epoch so direct/forwarded streams do not race independent transport recovery. Async collection, timing/load metrics, and typed request-path integration remain in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the typed physical-dispatch bridge required before BatchCommands can be selected by normal Rust request execution. It downcasts only the complete client-go `ToBatchCommandsRequest` command set after request mutation, clones the owned protobuf payload into the batch enum, and erases every accepted correlated response back into the same `Box<dyn Any>` carrier used by unary `KvClient::dispatch`. The source-excluded `RawChecksum` remains unbatchable. This is intentionally not yet wired into scheduling: source-compatible async collection/configuration must own when batchable requests are flushed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): BatchCommands dispatcher construction now consumes the source-mapped `TiKvClient` settings. A zero `max_batch_size` produces no dispatcher, matching client-go's disabled batching path; otherwise `max_batch_size` is its bounded queue capacity and `max_concurrency_request_limit` is its normal-priority admission limit. This establishes the configuration boundary, but the queued async worker that implements client-go's head collection, overload wait, and turbo wait remains required.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the owned bounded `BatchCommandsWorker`. It receives owned entries, runs the source-style head/drain/optional-wait collection operation, transfers only that collection into the dispatcher, and invokes the existing real stream publication/recovery path. The in-process Tonic stream regression now submits direct, forwarded, and post-reconnect work through this worker instead of calling `flush` manually. Normal `KvClient::dispatch` still does unary transport, so selecting this worker for eligible physical requests remains required before the client-go async path is transcreated.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the independent `internal/client/mockserver` test-support package. The test-only Rust façade starts, stops, and restarts a real loopback Tonic service; exposes exactly client-go's four implemented RPC routes; applies replaceable forwarding metadata checks; and supplies the dynamic/default BatchCommands response contract including health feedback sequence numbers. Generated server bindings are now an owned proto-build artifact. Its direct regression covers all routes, handler/error propagation, and lifecycle; the much larger parent `internal/client` consumer test suite remains in progress.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): `TikvConnect` now preserves the entire caller-supplied `TiKvClient` configuration alongside its extracted Tonic connection settings. Per-store BatchCommands worker creation therefore observes the configured enable/disable state, queue size, collection policy, overload threshold, and concurrency limit rather than rebuilding `TiKvClient::default()`. A loopback connector regression proves a configured zero batch size suppresses worker creation. Request-level forwarding ownership, metrics, and the remaining client lifecycle are still pending.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): repaired per-group BatchCommands flush failure ownership. Source `getClientAndSend` attempts its direct group and every forwarding group independently; the Rust seed previously returned on the first stream-open failure after moving the later groups out of the builder, which could strand their response futures. It now retires each failed group, continues the pass, and returns the first error after all groups have a terminal outcome. A regression uses two invalid forwarding metadata values to prove neither caller hangs.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the forwarding transport primitive to `KvRpcClient`. The new explicit forwarded-dispatch path routes batchable work into the host-specific stream and attaches client-go's `tikv-forwarded-host` metadata to supported unary RPCs; ordinary dispatch remains metadata-free. Every generated TiKV request implementation now preserves this boundary, including store-scoped commands and raw coprocessor delegation. A real mock-server regression proves both forwarded and direct unary behavior. The dynamic request wrapper still lacks its source `ForwardedHost` field, so no high-level plan selects this path yet.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected mockserver shutdown to match grpc-go `Server.Stop` rather than Tonic's graceful shutdown. Tonic detaches per-connection tasks, so aborting only its accept loop left live BatchCommands streams open. The test-only server now wraps each accepted TCP connection with a cancellation-aware I/O layer; `Stop` wakes every wrapper and forces Hyper to drop its connection. The regression holds an active bidirectional stream open, proves stop returns promptly, and observes terminal stream shutdown.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the pinned `internal/client` inventory. `client_fail.go` is not present at `52c1e76`; the failure artifact is `client_fail_test.go`. The inventory now also records package-local `OWNERS` as non-functional repository metadata. This does not alter implementation scope, but removes a false source artifact from the eventual atomic receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected Rust future-cancellation ownership in the integrated BatchCommands dispatch path. A `BatchCommandSubmission` now owns and marks its pre-selection cancellation token on drop, which is Rust's direct counterpart to `client_async.go`'s context `AfterFunc`: abandoning a dispatch future before builder selection makes `buildWithLimit` skip the entry without allocating an ID or sending an RPC. Post-publication cancellation still leaves ID retirement to the receive path. Focused BatchCommands (18) and store-client (5) tests pass on the pinned nightly; callback-executor-facing `SendRequestAsync` APIs and source timing/metrics remain unfinished parent-package work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): wired source `BatchCommandsResponse.transport_layer_load` through the Rust receive supervisor into the shared worker collection state. Subsequent collection passes now evaluate the source overload threshold against the last positive TiKV response load, rather than a hard-coded zero. The policy naturally ignores it when `max_batch_wait_time` is zero, matching Go's conditional use. The receive-loop regression proves a load of 42 is recorded; health-feedback listener callbacks and the remaining batch metrics are still separate unfinished source behavior.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the replaceable `ClientEventListener` boundary from `internal/client/client.go`. Clones of `KvRpcClient` share one listener slot, last registration wins, and each BatchCommands receive loop delivers an attached `HealthFeedback` before it demultiplexes request responses, matching the source ordering. The broader async-client/callback surface and metrics remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the `conn_pool.go` ownership audit. Rust already has an address-keyed `PdRpcClient.kv_client_cache`, shared by region/store mapping, so basic per-target reuse is present. The remaining source gap is versioned replacement (`CloseAddrVer`), client-wide close/idle-recycle lifecycle, and monitor semantics: Rust invalidation removes a cache entry without source pool versions or a close contract. Completing this requires extending that existing cache boundary, not relocating ownership above `PdRpcClient`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): traced the prerequisite for source `CloseAddrVer`. Rust transport errors are only generic `Grpc`/`GrpcAPI`; request retry invalidates by store ID and carries no address/generation. Client-go obtains `CloseAddrVer` inputs from typed `ErrConn{Addr, Ver}` errors produced at dispatch. A native typed connection-error carrier and its retry extraction path must therefore precede versioned cache invalidation; adding a local generation check alone would not be source-driven.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): repaired cancellation completion before BatchCommands request-ID assignment. The source context-cancellation callback settles a caller even when the batch builder later skips its canceled entry; Rust previously discarded the owned response sender in both `build_with_limit` and `reset`. Those paths now return a deterministic cancellation error and retain non-cancelled queued entries. Regressions cover cancellation selected during build and cancellation left unselected by a high-priority-only flush.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): `KvRpcClient::dispatch` now selects the worker only for the complete source batchable command set; all other requests stay unary. The bridge extracts the real protobuf `Context.resource_control_context.override_priority` for source high-priority admission instead of confusing ordinary command priority with resource control. Rust's current plan model has no forwarding-host field, so its normal dispatch represents the direct source path; forwarding remains confined to the explicit internal worker API until a plan-level forwarding contract is added.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the versioned connection-error and compare-close boundary from `internal/client`. `KvRpcClient` now wraps its transport failures in native `Error::Connection { address, version, source }`, the same information carried by client-go `ErrConn`; request retry identifies that carrier and asks the owning `PdRpcClient` cache to close only the matching-or-older generation. The cache retains a monotonically wrapping version per address, marks retired client clones closed, and serializes connection creation with compare-close so concurrent requests create one pool and a stale failure cannot remove a replacement. Focused regressions cover carrier fields, exact-old-generation eviction, and singleflight creation. This is still incremental: client-wide close/idle recycling, monitor metrics, async callback APIs, and dynamic forwarding selection remain unfinished `internal/client` work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): connected explicit generation retirement to the owned BatchCommands worker. A source-pool close now cancels collection, drains queued entries, retires every published response slot, and rejects later submissions with `batch client closed`; recoverable stream failures remain forwarding-host-scoped. This maps `connPool.Close`/`batchConn.Close` shutdown semantics rather than confusing shutdown with reconnection. The focused close regression passes. Client-wide owner APIs, idle recycling, monitor metrics, callback execution, and plan-level forwarding remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the owning `PdRpcClient::close` lifecycle counterpart to client-go `RPCClient.Close`. It atomically prevents new TiKV cache creation, drains every cached address pool, and invokes each concrete client close exactly once; repeated close is harmless and later lookup reports `rpc client is closed`. The focused lifecycle regression covers two pools and post-close lookup. Idle recycling, transport monitor metrics, public owning-client close exposure, callback execution, and high-level forwarding selection remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the observable idle-batch recycle boundary from `conn_batch.go`. An inactive Rust worker now retires its pool after the source three-minute timeout and makes the next dispatch take the existing connection-error replacement path; the short-timeout regression proves post-idle submissions are rejected. Connection identity is now a shared `KvRpcClient` clone slot, so workers created during connector construction observe the address/generation assigned later by `PdRpcClient`; the paired regression covers that construction order. Tonic still does not expose grpc-go's monitored connectivity states, so source connection-state gauges remain unimplemented.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the BatchCommands request-stage timing state from `client_batch.go`. Every entry now retains owned arrival/selection/send/first-response/receive timestamps through the pending-ID registry; source batch-wait, send-wait, recv-wait, and done observations are emitted on success, cancellation, timeout, stream failure, and explicit close. The physical protobuf receives `client_send_time_ns`, and the metric label uses `Context.peer.store_id`, as source does, instead of the pooled target. The native Prometheus crate exposes histograms rather than client-go's summary vector, so the mapping retains the source metric name, store/stage/result labels, and observations in a histogram vector. A source-derived boundary regression covers normal, terminal-before-send, timeout, and response-before-send-stamp normalization cases; the real generated-Tonic stream regression also asserts the emitted protobuf timestamp is nonzero. Stream tail/unavailability metrics, diagnostics, callback execution, and forwarding selection remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended the real in-process Tonic BatchCommands regression through `KvRpcClient::dispatch` itself. An ordinary `GetRequest` is selected by the normal physical dispatch path, transported on the generated bidirectional stream, and restored as its typed `GetResponse`; this runs alongside direct/forwarded worker submissions and recovery from a server-closed stream. It proves the direct normal request path is no longer merely an isolated batch seed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): began the source-owned RawKV retry migration. `RetryableMultiRegion` now accepts an owned retry state: legacy callers retain their attempt-count `Backoff`, while RawKV supplies a fresh 20,000-ms `RetryBackoffer` per multi-region operation. The plan forks one parent and one child per shard, cancels the parent child on the first terminal shard result, waits for all children, and merges accounting from the final completed child—matching `rawkv.sendBatchReq`/`sendBatchPut` rather than using a mutex-shared budget. Every RawKV multi-region request now selects this state; each scan page creates its own source budget, matching `sendReq`. The legacy Rust-only `with_backoff` builder is deprecated because client-go has no corresponding per-operation attempt-count override. Focused regressions prove an actual RawGet region miss retries, the per-shard fork/final-child merge topology, and sibling cancellation during cumulative backoff; the full pinned-nightly library suite passes 302 tests. This is incremental RawKV/request-plan evidence, not a RawKV package receipt: the source `internal/locate.RegionRequestSender` replica/error-classification path remains a separate prerequisite for complete request-path parity.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the BatchCommands receive-loop telemetry tail. Every direct/forwarded stream now observes source-labelled `batch_stream_recv_loop_duration_seconds` receive and process durations, 20-ms receive-loop tails, and 10-ms-or-greater TiKV-send-to-client tails. Reconnect success records the source unavailability histogram across its whole retry interval. Rust maps the two source summary vectors to histograms because the bundled Prometheus API does not provide summaries; metric names, labels, tail thresholds, and source histogram buckets are retained. The targeted delayed-stream regression asserts both tail classes, and the full library suite passes 303 tests. Request tracking/retirement counters, canceled-entry tails, slow/hang diagnostics, callbacks, and dynamic forwarding selection remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the owned stream-counter slice of BatchCommands metrics. Every published pending-response slot retains its source target, selected pool slot, and forwarding classification; registration increments `tracked`, successful response lookup increments `completed` and `retired`, missing response IDs increment `outdated`, and every send, stream, or explicit-close retirement increments `retired` from the slot itself. This prevents a later stream failure from guessing labels or charging a forwarding sibling. Focused regressions cover publication then ambiguous send failure (two tracked/two retired/one completed) and direct receive then host-local stream failure; the full pinned-nightly library suite remains green at 303 tests. Canceled-entry tail latency, slow/hang diagnostics, callbacks, and dynamic forwarding selection remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed BatchCommands cancelled-entry tail telemetry. A pending slot whose caller receiver has been dropped records the source `batch_stream_canceled_entry_tail_latency_seconds` observation only when its eventual TiKV response is received; the duration is response-receive minus batch-selection time, with the source 1-second-to-128-second histogram buckets and the retained stream labels. A focused dropped-receiver regression passes, and the pinned-nightly library suite passes 304 tests. Slow/hang diagnostics, callbacks, and dynamic forwarding selection remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): audited `client_async.go`'s callback boundary. `SendRequestAsync` exists because Go must return before an RPC completes; Rust's native `KvClient::dispatch` future is the equivalent completion handle and does not need a callback executor. Dropping that future before selection cancels the owned entry, while post-publication receiver drop retains source response retirement/tail accounting. Adding a detached callback façade would weaken that ownership contract, so callback execution is now an explicitly completed native API mapping rather than remaining work. The same pass transcreated the source pending-request diagnostic: once per minute the worker inspects 30-second slow and 90-second hanging entries, identifies the oldest, and uses a per-stream monotonic response-ID watermark to distinguish TiKV-unconfirmed entries. The five-entry source regression covers the exact slow/hanging and unconfirmed totals. Dynamic forwarding selection and source connection-state monitor gauges remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): aligned the pending-request inspection exit path with `conn_batch.go`. A worker now inspects outstanding published entries not only after its periodic collection pass but also immediately before an idle or closed loop retires the pool; this preserves the source's final slow/hang diagnostic opportunity without changing close retirement. The routing audit also establishes that plan-level forwarding cannot be added as an arbitrary host builder: client-go sets `ForwardedHost` only when `internal/locate` chooses a proxy replica, sends to the proxy address, and carries the selected target as metadata. That integration remains owned by the atomic `internal/locate` package transcreation.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the first full source inventory pass for `internal/locate`. The atomic Go package is 20,132 lines across production `accessmode.go` (62), `metrics_collector.go` (136), `pd_codec.go` (219), `region_cache.go` (3,472), `region_request.go` (2,449), `replica_selector.go` (744), `slow_score.go` (192), `sorted_btree.go` (151), and `store_cache.go` (1,222); tests/support are `main_test.go` (32), `metrics_collector_test.go` (157), `pd_codec_test.go` (40), `region_cache_test.go` (3,497), `region_request3_test.go` (1,800), `region_request_state_test.go` (769), `region_request_test.go` (1,274), and `replica_selector_test.go` (3,916). There is no package-local generated source, fixture, build selection, or `doc.go`. Current Rust `region.rs`, `region_cache.rs`, `pd/*`, `request/{plan,plan_builder,shard}.rs`, and `store/*` contain compatible seeds only. Completion must jointly own region/store cache lifetime, PD codecs, access modes, slow-score/health feedback, replica selection/proxy routing, `RegionRequestSender` retry/error state, runtime metrics, cancellation, and every source test artifact; no partial dynamic-forwarding integration is dispatched ahead of that receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected two `config/retry.Backoffer` error-boundary details. Rust now formats a pre-cancelled or noop backoff as the triggering reason itself, matching Go's returned error rather than adding a native wrapper prefix. If cancellation occurs after a sleep has begun, it records a zero-duration retry and returns success for that call; the next invocation observes cancellation, exactly as the source `time.After` select does. Regressions cover both formatting and in-flight accounting. Consumer migration to source-owned cumulative retry budgets remains required before a `config/retry` receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the source max-budget scaling and diagnostic-string details in `config/retry`. `BackOffWeight` now applies only when multiplication remains within Go's signed `MaxInt32` guard, so the BatchCommands reconnect budget keeps its source `math.MaxInt32` value instead of being silently doubled. `RetryBackoffer` also renders the source ` backoff(<total>ms [<types>])` form, including the leading space and empty pre-sleep string. Regressions cover both boundaries. Consumer-wide cumulative-budget ownership still prevents an atomic package receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added isolated source-derived `internal/locate` foundations: `AccessMode`/`ReplicaFlowsType` display contracts plus the concurrent `slow_score.go` moving windows and score state. The periodic update retains source compare-and-swap ownership, preventing it from replacing a newer concurrent slow score. The source sorted-region index is deliberately not implemented in isolation: its B-tree entries own the complete cached `Region` TTL/version lifecycle, so it must arrive with region-cache integration. The scoped pinned-nightly `locate` suite passes four regressions; this is seed evidence only, not a package receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): strengthened the existing Rust ordered region cache toward `regionIndexMu.insertRegionToCache`. `add_region` now returns the source acceptance decision, rejects a delayed lower region/conf epoch, preserves the latest-ID map through replacement, and treats an empty cached end key as positive infinity while removing intersecting entries. A regression covers delayed same-ID PD data and max-end intersections. TTL refresh/GC, store epochs, replica state, and all request-sender behavior remain mandatory for the atomic `internal/locate` receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): integrated the source region-cache TTL lookup contract into Rust's ordered cache. Cached entries now carry a default 600-second TTL with `[0, 60)` jitter; key, end-key, and ID reads reject entries strictly past expiry and refresh a live, non-forced entry when it enters the source renewal window. The deterministic regression proves an entry at its TTL boundary renews while an expired entry forces a PD reload. Background bounded GC and `needExpireAfterTTL` transitions from store health remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the dependency-free `StoreHealthStatus` state from `store_cache.go` as an isolated `internal/locate` seed. It combines the existing client slow-score stat with TiKV feedback, preserves the source 100-ms feedback update gate, 15-second stale-feedback check, `20/60`-per-second linear decay to one, and the shared slow threshold. Deterministic regressions cover gated updates, decay, and client/server combination. It intentionally has no active `GetHealthFeedback` callback or store-cache attachment until the complete store lifecycle owns liveness and scheduler behavior.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): attached the health state to the existing Rust cached-store ownership boundary. Region-cache stores now retain protobuf metadata plus one shared `StoreHealthStatus`; stream-style `HealthFeedback` updates only its matching cached store and drops unknown IDs, matching source `RegionCache.onHealthFeedback`. The test proves ownership and slow-score visibility. Client event-listener registration, periodic ticks/active refresh, liveness, and selector consumption remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the source event path from a production KV connection to the cached store health state. `KvClient` now has a default listener-registration hook; concrete `KvRpcClient` installs it, and the real `PdRpcClient<..., Cluster>` registers the shared region-cache listener when mapping regions or enumerating stores. The listener applies feedback synchronously, preserving client-go's receive-before-response-demux ordering; weak ownership prevents it from retaining a closed region cache. Generic/mock transports retain a no-op hook. The full pinned-nightly library suite (316 tests) passes. Periodic health ticking, active feedback refresh, store liveness, and replica-selection consumption remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the cache-owned periodic health tick. It snapshots the shared health handles under the cached-store lock and ticks them after releasing it, so TiKV feedback decays through the same store-owned state a selector will read. The regression drives a score of 40 through 15 seconds to source value 35. Scheduling cadence, active `GetHealthFeedback`, and liveness predicates remain deferred to the complete store-cache lifecycle.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended cached stores with source `livenessState` (`reachable`, `unreachable`, `unknown`) and preserved that state plus `StoreHealthStatus` when fresh PD metadata replaces address/labels. New stores default reachable, as Go's zero-valued liveness field does; the state is now available to the future selector. This is not yet an active health-check/re-resolve implementation, and no source store epoch or tombstone lifecycle is claimed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the pure mixed-replica scoring foundation from `replica_selector.go`. It preserves the source bit priority `NotSlow > LabelMatches > PreferLeader > NormalPeer > NotAttempted`, candidate liveness/attempt filtering, prefer-leader slow-follower exclusion, and learner-mode normal-peer distinction. The regression exposed and retains the source behavior that a matching-label non-learner can outrank a learner. This seed deliberately stops before random tie selection, per-attempt flags, request mutation, proxy forwarding, and cache invalidation.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): connected source mixed-selector inputs to real Rust cache state. `RegionCache::replica_candidates` resolves region peers through cached stores and snapshots leader identity, learner role, caller labels, slow score, liveness, and selector-owned attempt counters without holding a lock over PD access. The deterministic regression covers leader/follower role, labels, unreachable state, and attempts. Down-peer/witness filtering, random tie selection, RPC contexts, and proxy forwarding remain in the larger selector/send state machine.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed source random tie handling for the mixed-selector seed. `MixedReplicaSelection::choose` selects uniformly from the exact highest-score ties, while unique-score regressions remain deterministic. It does not make the seed a request-path selector: target connection selection, attempt/error flags, request mutation, and forwarding still belong to the larger state machine.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): began connecting `internal/locate` selection to Rust's ordinary request path. `RegionStore` now preserves the logical selected peer independently from the cached leader, physical RPC target, and optional forwarding host. Every region-sharded request derives its protobuf `Context.peer` from that logical peer; `Dispatch` invokes forwarding-aware transport only when its route carries a host. This mirrors `buildRPCContext` plus the `sendToAddr`/`ForwardedHost` split: direct follower reads carry a follower peer with no forwarding metadata, while only a proxy route carries the logical target address as metadata. No selector currently constructs a non-leader route, so this is plumbing, not an `internal/locate` receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): connected the cache-side mixed selector to concrete peer metadata. `RegionCache::select_mixed_replica` resolves all region stores before snapshotting health/liveness/labels, applies the source score and random-tie policy outside cache locks, then returns the actual selected `metapb::Peer`. The regression proves a healthy follower is returned for follower mode while cached leader metadata remains unchanged. This still lacks selector-owned retry/error state and an API path that asks `PdRpcClient` to open the selected store connection.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added that route-construction boundary in `PdRpcClient::map_region_to_route`. It resolves the logical target store and, optionally, a physical proxy store; opens/reuses the physical connection; puts the selected peer in `RegionStore`; and sets `forwarded_host` exactly when a proxy was selected (not by comparing addresses). The ordinary `PdClient::map_region_to_store` now uses the same direct-leader route builder. This makes cache selection consumable by a future source selector while preserving direct leader behavior. Snapshot/read configuration and the selector's retry/error/proxy choice state are still required.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the stable request-level replica-selection carrier. `ReplicaReadConfig` lives on `Dispatch`, is copied by shard clones and forwarded through retry wrappers, and causes `RetryableMultiRegion` to ask PD for a source-selected route. The concrete PD client uses cache-backed mixed selection for non-leader modes; generic PD clients retain direct leader mapping. Region-sharded protobufs now set `Context.replica_read` iff the selected logical peer differs from the cached leader, while context-free store commands remain no-ops. This is deliberately lower-layer work: `Snapshot` has not yet exposed `SetReplicaRead`, request-local attempt/error state and proxy selection are still absent, and no package receipt is claimed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): exposed the source-shaped snapshot entry point: `Snapshot::set_replica_read(ReplicaReadType)`. It replaces the snapshot transaction's default leader config, so Get, BatchGet, and scan requests built through the common transaction plan helper retain the setting through shard/retry construction. `set_replica_read_config` remains an explicit advanced form for stable selector constraints. Ordinary transactions still initialize the config to leader, and write/heartbeat callers explicitly retain direct leader behavior. Stale-read flags, replica-read seed/adjuster semantics, and selector-local retry/error transitions remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the first-attempt stale-read route/context contract. A stale `ReplicaReadConfig` selects as `Mixed`, retains a distinct `RegionStore.stale_read` bit, sets `Context.stale_read`, and forces `Context.replica_read` false even when the logical peer is a follower. `Snapshot::set_stale_read` owns that stable setting. This deliberately stops before source stale-read retry behavior: resolving a lock disables stale read, the second retry probes the leader, and error state changes remain selector-owned work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): connected source leader forwarding to the production PD route. `PdRpcClient` retains `Config.enable_forwarding`; when the cached leader is explicitly unreachable, `RegionCache` picks a reachable non-leader proxy and `map_region_to_route` opens that physical connection while retaining the leader peer and leader address as the logical context/forwarded host. Unknown liveness intentionally does not enable proxying. This is the safe core of `ReplicaSelectLeaderWithProxyStrategy`, not its complete retry/proxy-cache algorithm.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the source `KVSnapshot.SetMatchStoreLabels` boundary to both async and synchronous snapshots. It replaces `ReplicaReadConfig.labels` while preserving the current read type and stale setting. Those labels feed the source-compatible cache score; `WithMatchStores` is likewise a score preference rather than an eligibility filter. Read-replica scope and read-adjuster/load-threshold APIs remain separate unimplemented snapshot inputs.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): connected source client-side slow-score recording for prefer-leader reads. `map_region_to_route` attaches the logical target store's shared health status; only routes created from `ReplicaReadPreferLeader` enable timing in `Dispatch`, so elapsed physical-RPC time is recorded against that logical store even through a forwarding proxy. Ordinary, follower, and stale reads do not mutate client-side slow score through this path. Active server feedback refresh and liveness probing remain cache-lifecycle work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): replaced the Rust boolean region-error result with an explicit retry action, preserving client-go's error-class backoff selection in the retryable multi-region path and RawKV scan loop. Server-is-busy now marks the logical store slow and uses `BoTiKVServerBusy`; disk full, recovery, witness, scheduling, stale command, max-ts, and region-initializing errors preserve their respective source retry classes. Flashback, undetermined result, and raft-entry-too-large remain terminal. This is still not a complete `internal/locate` selector: per-selector attempted-peer/error flags, busy-leader probing, stale second-attempt fallback, and proxy rotation remain required.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added an internal `ReplicaSelectorState` carried by `Dispatch` clones, not by public `ReplicaReadConfig`. It preserves peer-attempt counts across retry-plan reshards, passes those counts into source mixed selection, and records `DataIsNotReady` to allow one additional follower attempt. On the second stale-read selector attempt an untried leader is mapped as a normal leader read, matching client-go's fallback. Not-leader/error flags, busy-leader suspect probing, replica load/seed adjustment, and source proxy rotation are still incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the source `ServerIsBusy(0)` cached-leader workaround. Two zero-estimated-wait failures for the same direct leader mark a per-request probe; the next leader route selects an untried follower but explicitly suppresses `Context.replica_read`, so the follower receives a leader read and can return a real `NotLeader` hint. The state resets when the cached leader changes, and no follower probe occurs for leader-only, stale, non-leader-mode, or nonzero-estimate busy errors. Per-replica busy/load thresholds and the remaining selector flags still need complete transcreation.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): a concrete `NotLeader` leader hint now changes the internal selector state to leader mode when the hinted peer has not already been attempted. The next `PdRpcClient` route resolves the hinted store and requires source-equivalent reachable liveness before following cached leader/proxy behavior rather than continuing the original mixed/follower mode. A same-peer, already-attempted, or unreachable hint does not force the transition. Every remaining source candidate flag still needs complete integration.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): cached stores now retain source `ServerIsBusy.estimated_wait_ms` load statistics. `RegionCache` records the reported wait with a monotonic timestamp and returns the optimistic decayed remaining wait used by client-go's `EstimatedWaitTime`. The retry handler feeds nonzero busy estimates through the `PdClient` cache owner; custom clients remain a no-op. Configurable busy-threshold request context and idle-replica selection have not yet been transcreated, so this is the prerequisite signal rather than a complete load-aware selector.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the first configurable busy-threshold path. `ReplicaReadConfig.busy_threshold_ms` propagates through `RegionStore` into every context-bearing TiKV request. For a leader route whose cached remaining wait exceeds that threshold, `PdRpcClient` chooses an unattempted reachable idle follower through the source mixed score. Nonzero `ServerIsBusy` also marks its peer selector-locally busy; if no idle follower remains, the leader route persists a zero busy threshold for later retries, matching source all-busy fallback. Source request-kind gating and other selector flags remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added client-go's guarded `FlashbackInProgress` selector transition. When the physical route is a normal replica read, the retry is immediate, forces the untried reachable leader, and clears busy-threshold state. Direct leader reads and stale/forced-leader reads retain the terminal flashback error, while `FlashbackNotPrepared` remains terminal in every case. This is only the selector transition; full source flashback request orchestration is outside `internal/locate`.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): exposed the source `KVSnapshot.SetLoadBasedReplicaReadThreshold` API on both async and synchronous Rust snapshots. Its value reaches the existing `ReplicaReadConfig.busy_threshold_ms` selector/context path in milliseconds; zero durations and values above TiKV's `u32` wire-field bound disable the feature, matching client-go. `ReplicaReadSeed` remains deliberately unmodeled in selection because source request plumbing retains it but the pinned selector does not consume it. This is incremental `txnkv/txnsnapshot` and `internal/locate` evidence, not either package's completion receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): mapped `RegionRequestSender.onRegionNotFound`'s request-local exception. Rust now hard-invalidates the shared region cache but, only when its cached leader has not yet been attempted, preserves selector state for one immediate leader retry rather than consuming `BoRegionMiss`; an already-attempted leader follows the ordinary invalidation/backoff path. This deliberately does not borrow flashback's threshold clearing. The source state transition has a focused regression; complete sender invalidation/liveness behavior remains unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added a native `ReplicaReadAdjuster` mapping for `KVSnapshot.SetReplicaReadAdjuster`. The callback receives the actual unresolved key count for each Get or BatchGet, returns a new read type plus zero or one source-shaped selector option (labels, store IDs, leader-only, or prefer-leader), and adjusts a cloned request config only when the stable setting is follower-mode. Existing snapshot settings therefore remain unchanged for later reads; scans deliberately do not invoke it because the pinned Go scan path does not. This is incremental snapshot/selector work, not a package receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): threaded source `isReadReq` classification through Rust's request, sharding, and PD routing seams. Load-based leader-to-idle-follower selection now runs only for transactional Get, BatchGet, Scan, and coprocessor commands; writes and RawKV requests do not opt in merely because a generic configuration exists. A coprocessor request with preassigned per-store tasks is separately identified so a busy response cannot mark it for replica redirection, matching the source guard against turning fixed task batches into region misses. Full Cop response-control-flow and complete sender state remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): mapped the stale-read lock fallback from `KVSnapshot.get`. `ResolveLock` now mutates only its retry clone when a lock is observed: `stale_read` clears, read type becomes leader, and `BusyThresholdMs` becomes zero before lock resolution retries. The original immutable wrapper remains safe for sibling plans. The behavior is available through all existing shard wrappers and has a focused Dispatch-state regression. Complete stale-read snapshot/scan retry choreography remains part of the unfinished sender package.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated the successful side of `replicaSelector.onSendSuccess` for the existing forced leader-read probe. If a follower physically serves a leader-context probe successfully, Rust best-effort updates the cached region leader to that logical peer; an advisory cache-update failure never changes the successful RPC result. Ordinary replica/stale reads cannot promote their target. Source transport-failure liveness probing and proxy cache rotation remain separate unfinished store-cache work.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): stale-read retry state now mirrors the source leader-attempt gate. If stale routing returns to mixed selection after the leader has already been attempted and is not busy, the selected follower uses normal replica-read context rather than stale-read context. The first route remains stale and the second-attempt untried-leader fallback remains a normal leader read. Source's first-attempt label-mismatch exception and full request seed/adjuster behavior remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): transcreated `RegionCache.OnRegionEpochNotMatch`'s cache-refresh core. When TiKV includes replacement metadata, Rust now invalidates the old cache entry only if no replacement has its exact version, seeds each replacement's provisional leader from the responding store, carries the previous bucket metadata into each replacement, and inserts every replacement through the existing stale-safe region index. A source-ahead epoch still takes the existing `BoRegionMiss` path without cache mutation. The TiFlash electable-store special case is not modeled because Rust has no distinct TiFlash route model; complete request-sender/store-cache parity remains open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the direct `BucketVersionNotMatch` cache path from `internal/locate`. `RegionWithLeader` now retains PD bucket metadata; its version reaches every context-bearing request after sharding, and a mismatch replaces only older cached metadata. The PD codec decodes bucket boundaries for callers and re-encodes decoded error metadata before caching, preserving Rust's existing encoded-cache boundary. As in client-go, the sender refreshes the cache but propagates the mismatch to the bucket-aware caller rather than retrying it generically. PD `need_buckets` lookup options, bucket-aware range splitting/rescheduling, asynchronous version refresh, and TiFlash-specific routing remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): aligned the existing all-store refresh with `RegionCache.GetAllStores`: it now keeps both TiKV and TiFlash stores while excluding tombstones and TiFlash-compute nodes. This makes TiFlash discovery visible through the existing PD all-store API, but does not add a TiFlash endpoint request API, peer load balancing/failure rotation, or the separate TiFlash-compute lifecycle.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): preserved the source `accessMode` separation after exposing TiFlash stores. Rust's ordinary replica selector now builds candidates only from TiKV peers; a cached TiFlash peer is never eligible for a transactional leader/follower/stale route. TiFlash endpoint routing remains absent, so this is a correctness guard on the existing TiKV path rather than a TiFlash implementation.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected and covered the remaining deterministic `internal/resourcecontrol` response cases. `GetResponse` and `BatchGetResponse` use their V2 scan and KV-CPU details, while `ScanResponse` charges its encoded response size as client-go does when no execution details are available. Coprocessor CPU accounting now also falls back to legacy `ExecDetails.TimeDetail` if V2 data is absent, preserving the source precedence. Legacy and `nextgen` focused runs both validate the intentional processed-versus-max(total, processed) scan-byte distinction; the full pinned-nightly library suite passes 351 tests. Generic request wrapper extraction, bypass/access mapping, controller interception, and transport integration remain unclaimed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): aligned two `internal/locate.RegionRequestSender.onRegionError` stop conditions. `StoreNotMatch` and `MismatchPeerId` now invalidate Rust cache state but return the received region error instead of incorrectly consuming `BoRegionMiss` and retrying the same send loop. This preserves source caller-visible recovery and leaves later requests to rebuild their routes. The focused regression, request suite (50 tests), and full pinned-nightly library suite (352 tests) pass. Store re-resolution epochs, connection closing, active liveness checks, and the rest of the sender lifecycle remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected `NotLeader` cache acceptance to the source selector contract. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): modeled client-go sender outcomes that consume a retry class but deliberately end the current loop. `RecoveryInProgress` and `IsWitness` now back off once then return their region error, while `KeyNotInRegion` invalidates and returns immediately; they no longer retry as generic region misses. The focused regression, request suite (51 tests), and full pinned-nightly library suite (353 tests) pass. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): an earlier audit incorrectly treated the non-selector fallback as the TiKV selector path for an unclassified region error. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): made `EpochNotMatch` outcome explicit. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): aligned `ServerIsBusy` selector retry timing. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): aligned source `StaleCommand` selector behavior. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): retained the source hintless-`NotLeader` state. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended the source `internal/resourcecontrol.MakeRequestInfo` seed to Rust's typed request boundary. Plan revision note (2026-08-23, corrected 2026-08-24): implemented the exhausted-leader selector transition from `nextForReplicaReadLeader`. At that boundary Rust probes an eligible follower with leader-read context (`replica_read=false`); a configurable read deadline instead uses genuine follower-read context, while hintless `NotLeader` retains the leader-read probe after scheduling backoff. `leader_only` returns to the sender/cache-refresh path when no candidate remains. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added the `onReadReqConfigurableTimeout` retry gate. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the `internal/client` ledger after auditing the actual dynamic request path. `Dispatch::apply_store` already retains both the physical proxy target and logical forwarded host supplied by `RegionStore`; its execution path calls `dispatch_with_forwarded_host`. Plan revision note (2026-08-24): integrated the `internal/resourcecontrol` seed at Rust's physical `Dispatch` boundary. The reusable controller applies client-go's selection (nonempty resource group, non-background, non-bypass), request wait, penalty, and only-if-unset override priority before ordinary RPC interceptors and transport dispatch; it receives response settlement only for a non-error response. Plan revision note (2026-08-24): completed the next resource-control integration slice. Plan revision note (2026-08-24): filled the remaining route-accounting fields from `internal/locate.RegionRequestSender.send`. `RegionStore` counts only voter and learner peers (with source empty-metadata fallback), and concrete PD routing maps `Config.zone_label` plus the selected logical store's `zone` label to local/cross/unknown access location. `Dispatch` keeps those values across shard clones and gives them to resource-control request information. Focused role/zone and selection regressions pass. Predicted read bytes, RU-details ownership, raw-client configuration, and a concrete PD controller remain incomplete.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): transcreated the source `internal/locate` per-store request token gate. `PdRpcClient` applies `TiKvClient.store_limit` to the process-wide source setting and owns one shared atomic count for each logical TiKV store selected for a region route. Before admission/interceptors/transport, Dispatch uses client-go's intentionally non-CAS check-then-increment and returns the source `TokenLimitError` when the observed count reaches the configured positive limit. Its RAII guard releases the token after success, transport failure, or response-decode failure. Source all-store broadcasts bypass `RegionRequestSender` and deliberately remain unlimited. Focused regressions cover rejection/release and region-route propagation; the source limit-exceeded metric remains unimplemented. This is `internal/locate` seed evidence only, not a package receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): completed the source token-limit observability boundary. Rejected region requests now increment `tikv_client_go_get_store_limit_token_error_total` with the source `address` and `store` labels. Direct routes use the selected transport address, while forwarded routes use their logical forwarded host as `Store.GetAddr()` does. The focused rejection regression proves the labeled counter advances with the returned `TokenLimitError`; `internal/locate` remains seed evidence pending its full package receipt.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): propagated client-go's optional `tikvrpc.Request.PredictedReadBytes` through Rust's native dynamic `Dispatch` wrapper. `PlanBuilder::predicted_read_bytes` preserves the hint across sharding and retry clones and supplies it to resource-control admission only for reads; transactional and raw writes retain the source zero value. The resource-control selection regression covers both branches. Concrete PD-controller paging policy remains outside this seed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): added source `RUDetails.Update` accounting to resource-controlled physical dispatches. `RuDetails` now accumulates read RU, write RU, and wait duration independently of its existing RU-v2 counters; `PlanBuilder::ru_details` shares that handle across all shard/retry clones. Dispatch records successful admission and response-settlement consumption in source order, while transport failures retain their existing no-settlement behavior. Plan revision note (2026-08-24): completed transaction-side RU-details ownership. Plan revision note (2026-08-24): exposed the same RU-details handle on async and synchronous snapshots. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): started the source `replicaSelector.onSendFailure` liveness boundary. Each `RegionStore` now keeps the physical destination store ID and endpoint type separately from its logical request peer, so forwarded leader requests probe the actual proxy. On a concrete PdRpcClient TiKV transport failure, Rust opens the standard `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` route under the configured client-go `store-liveness-timeout`; `SERVING`, `UNKNOWN`/`SERVICE_UNKNOWN`, and non-serving/transport outcomes map to the matching source liveness states. The sender preserves its cached region for this concrete path, allowing attempt/liveness selector state to choose the retry. A one-second single-flight loop continues probing an unhealthy TiKV store, re-resolves its PD metadata every 30 seconds while retaining the old liveness state, and stops when it recovers or the client closes. Source store-epoch snapshots and exact connection cancellation behavior remain unfinished; no `internal/locate` receipt is claimed.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): added source store failure epochs to the liveness path. A cached region records every peer store's epoch at insertion; a non-reachable physical destination CAS-advances that store only if its failed route owns the recorded epoch, then marks the source health state slow. Replica selection excludes peers whose captured epoch is stale; an epoch-stale leader enters the existing follower fallback instead of being sent again. A focused cache regression proves atomic one-time epoch advancement and stale-peer rejection; the full pinned-nightly library suite passes 364 tests. Exact sender/cache invalidation branches, metrics, and the full package inventory remain unfinished.

Plan revision note (2026-08-23): extended `replicaSelector.onReadReqConfigurableTimeout` to TiKV's region-error form. A source read whose execution duration is below 30 seconds now immediately reselects when `ServerIsBusy.reason` contains `deadline is exceeded`; it bypasses Rust busy bookkeeping and `BoTiKVServerBusy`, as client-go does before invoking `onServerIsBusy`. Other busy reasons and durations at or above the boundary retain the ordinary selector/backoff path. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): completed the remaining source timeout spelling in `onRegionError`. A short configurable read now immediately reselects when the otherwise-unclassified protobuf message contains `Deadline is exceeded`; the predicate excludes every typed error branch that client-go handles first, including `ServerIsBusy`. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected the generic selector recursion boundary. A bounded unknown-error and ServerIsBusy first-error/second-success regression proves exactly one shard is retained and two RPC attempts occur in both immediate and post-backoff cases. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): applied the same source boundary to transport send failures. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected non-selector flashback terminal errors. `FlashbackInProgress` and `FlashbackNotPrepared` now return the same direct field-specific messages as client-go rather than a generic protobuf region-error wrapper; the existing replica-read forced-leader retry remains earlier in the state machine. Plan revision note (2026-08-23): corrected `RaftEntryTooLarge` terminal identity. Zero or one uses client-go's default 256-pair scanner batch. Focused forward and reverse wire regressions cover request limits, continuation boundaries, and ordered results. Runtime stats, the source iterator API/callback ownership, and the atomic receipt remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): added the physical-RPC core of `KVSnapshot.SetRuntimeStats`. Clone and merge retain source-style independent snapshots. Backoff, TiKV execution-detail, resolve-lock, and read-pool statistics remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): extended snapshot runtime stats with the response execution details client-go merges for point and batch reads. The collector merges V2 (or legacy) TiKV time detail and every `ScanDetailV2` field from Get, BatchGet, and BufferBatchGet before decoding, retaining exact V2-over-legacy precedence through clone/merge. The generated pinned protobuf has no scan-response execution-detail field, matching the source scanner's lack of `mergeExecDetail` there. Backoff, resolve-lock, read-pool detail, and exact source formatting remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): snapshot runtime stats now time `resolve_lock_for_read` exactly around Rust's source-shaped read resolver call, including error returns and excluding retry sleep. The collector is deliberately absent from mutation lock resolution. A locked Get regression delays `CheckTxnStatus` and proves the same snapshot collector records the resolution duration and both physical Get attempts. Backoff detail, unavailable read-pool protobuf detail, and exact source formatting remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): snapshot region reads now use the source 20,000-ms input `RetryBackoffer` rather than the legacy fixed-attempt schedule. Forks retain cumulative accounting and sibling cancellation; the native no-resolve option remains a terminal no-retry boundary. Runtime stats copy each source retry class/scheduled sleep from that owner. The server-busy regression now observes client-go's 1–2-second equal-jitter first delay. Read-lock `txnLockFast` still uses the older Rust `Backoff` and remains open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): snapshot read-lock waits now use client-go's 20,000-ms cumulative `RetryBackoffer` and `BackoffWithMaxSleepTxnLockFast` behavior. Each `txnLockFast` wait is capped to the resolver's remaining TTL, while a zero TTL immediately reissues the read; the runtime collector records the retry class and scheduled sleep. Mutation lock resolution deliberately retains the native legacy backoff. The focused live-lock Get regression proves a one-millisecond TTL cap. The source iterator/callback ownership and atomic package receipt remain open.

Plan revision note (2026-08-24): added native stateful snapshot scanners. `SnapshotIterator` and `SyncSnapshotIterator` retain one scan batch, exclusive forward `NextKey(last)` or reverse upper-bound continuation, terminal validity, and explicit close; each refill uses the snapshot's configured batch size and full read/retry configuration. `Snapshot` is now generic over `PdClient` with the existing production default, allowing the iterator to be tested through the mock transport.
